reason: B offers the more physically plausible route at 600 °C because an oxidation-generated Ag-containing nanocomposite tribolayer can remain protective, whereas A relies on ethanol-derived amorphous carbon and sulfide nanoflakes that may oxidize or degrade in hot air and largely repeats the cited spray-coating work. B is clearly falsifiable and extends reactive wear protection toward broad-temperature friction control, although its claimed friction reduction and self-healing behavior remain insufficiently supported.
